classification.difficultyReason: Derive the annuity-due series, rearrange for a contribution and solve a scaffolded exponential threshold, selecting the smallest qualifying integer.

content.prompt: The company that Itsushi works for makes contributions to his superannuation scheme on 1st January each year. Any amount invested in this scheme earns interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Let $M$ be the annual contribution. Show that the value of the investment at the end of the $n$th year is
$$A_n=\frac{M\times1.075\times(1.075^n-1)}{0.075}.$$

answer.short: The contributions form a geometric series with first term $M(1.075)$, common ratio $1.075$ and $n$ terms, so $A_n=\frac{M(1.075)(1.075^n-1)}{0.075}$.
answer.worked:
Contributions are made on 1 January.

End of 1st year: $M(1.075)$.

End of 2nd year: $M(1.075)^2+M(1.075)$.

At the end of the $n$th year:
$$A_n=M(1.075)^n+M(1.075)^{n-1}+\cdots+M(1.075).$$
This is a geometric series with first term $M(1.075)$, common ratio $1.075$ and $n$ terms.
$$\begin{align*}A_n&=\frac{M(1.075)(1.075^n-1)}{1.075-1}\\A_n&=\frac{M(1.075)(1.075^n-1)}{0.075}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Itsushi plans to have $\$1\,500\,000$ in superannuation when he retires in 25 years’ time. Show that the company must contribute $\$20\,526.52$ each year, correct to the nearest cent.

answer.short: $M=\$20\,526.52$ per year, to the nearest cent.
answer.worked:
For 25 years:
$$A_{25}=M(1.075)^{25}+M(1.075)^{24}+\cdots+M(1.075).$$
Using the geometric-series result:
$$\begin{align*}1\,500\,000&=\frac{M(1.075)(1.075^{25}-1)}{0.075}\\M&=\frac{1\,500\,000(0.075)}{1.075(1.075^{25}-1)}\\M&\approx\$20\,526.52.\end{align*}$$
The company must contribute $\$20\,526.52$ each year, to the nearest cent.

children.label: d
children.prompt:
Show that $n$ is the smallest integer solution of
$$(1.075)^n>\frac{750000\times0.075}{20526.52\times1.075}+1.$$

answer.short: $\frac{20526.52(1.075)(1.075^n-1)}{0.075}>750000$ rearranges to the required inequality; the first qualifying year is its smallest integer solution.
answer.worked:
Using the geometric-series formula from part (a):
$$\begin{align*}\frac{20526.52(1.075)(1.075^n-1)}{0.075}&>750000\\1.075^n-1&>\frac{750000(0.075)}{20526.52(1.075)}\\1.075^n&>\frac{750000(0.075)}{20526.52(1.075)}+1.\end{align*}$$
The balance increases each year, so the first year above $\$750\,000$ is the smallest integer satisfying this inequality.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Evaluate the right-hand side to four decimal places.

answer.short: The right-hand side is $3.549169630\ldots$, which rounds to $3.5492$.
answer.worked:
$$\frac{750000(0.075)}{20526.52(1.075)}+1=3.549169630\ldots\approx3.5492.$$
The right-hand side is $3.5492$ to four decimal places. Use the unrounded threshold from part (d) to find the smallest integer year.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Use logarithms or trial-and-error to find the value of $n$.

answer.short: $n=18$; he changes jobs in the 18th year.
answer.worked:
Using the unrounded threshold from part (d):
$$\begin{align*}n&>\frac{\log\left(\frac{750000(0.075)}{20526.52(1.075)}+1\right)}{\log(1.075)}\\n&>17.515\ldots\end{align*}$$
The smallest integer solution is $n=18$. Itsushi changes jobs in the 18th year.
